dimensions.assessment: Affects researchers, developers, institutions, and members of the public utilizing federal health data sets.
dimensions.evidence: allows individuals to search, sort, and download the data sets made available through such website at no cost

dimensions.assessment: Administrative and operational changes for HHS to consolidate and maintain public data sets via standardized APIs and bulk downloads.
dimensions.evidence: create on the internet website opendata.hhs.gov... a repository of all publicly available data sets generated or maintained by the Department

dimensions.assessment: Requires HHS to implement web infrastructure and annual reporting, though no specific funding authorization amount is stated.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall submit to Congress a report

dimensions.assessment: Mandates a new consolidated web repository, API accessibility, and annual reporting on data availability and constraints.
dimensions.evidence: is accessible through standardized application programming interfaces that permit automated, machine-to-machine retrieval

dimensions.assessment: Permanent requirement for HHS to maintain the repository and submit ongoing annual reports to Congress.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter

missing_information: Any specific budget allocations or cost estimates for building and maintaining the website are absent.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services to create a centralized, machine-readable public data repository on opendata.hhs.gov within one year, impacting public data access and agency reporting.
